package_info.why_malicious: The package is a typosquat of the legitimate 'ionicons' package and contains obfuscated JavaScript code that exfiltrates end-user form data to attacker-controlled domains. Its sole purpose is to deceive developers into installing it and to steal sensitive user information from applications that include it, violating user privacy and application security.

execution_context.file_location: main package JavaScript file (e.g., index.js or distributed bundle)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code attaches 'submit' event listeners to all form elements in the DOM, collects the submitted form data, and sends it via HTTPS POST to a hardcoded attacker-controlled domain (ionicio.com), resulting in exfiltration of sensitive user input.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code intercepts all form submissions and exfiltrates user-provided data to an external, attacker-controlled domain without user consent or legitimate purpose. This behavior is highly indicative of credential theft or data harvesting.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate icon package should only provide static assets or rendering logic for icons and should not interact with the DOM, attach event listeners to forms, or perform network requests on form submissions.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate analytics or form-handling libraries may collect form data, but only with explicit user consent and send it to trusted, well-known domains. They do not use obfuscated code or target unrelated domains, especially those mimicking legitimate package names.
key_indicators: Obfuscated JavaScript code targeting all form elements in the DOM
Attaches 'submit' event listeners to every form on the page
Collects form data using FormData API
Sends HTTPS POST requests to a hardcoded, attacker-controlled domain (ionicio.com) that is a typosquat of the legitimate vendor
No legitimate reason for an icon package to access or exfiltrate form data

attack_chain.action: Developer installs the malicious package (icon-package) instead of the legitimate one due to typosquatting.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is included in the application bundle.

attack_chain.action: When the application runs in a user's browser, the malicious code executes and attaches 'submit' event listeners to all form elements in the DOM.
attack_chain.leads_to: Form submissions are intercepted by the malicious code.

attack_chain.action: On form submission, the code collects all form data and sends it via HTTPS POST to the attacker's domain (ionicio.com).
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltration of sensitive user data to the attacker-controlled infrastructure.

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code in UI or icon packages that attaches 'submit' event listeners to all form elements in the DOM
Obfuscated code that interacts with the DOM and collects form data using the FormData API
Network requests to domains that are typosquats of legitimate package vendor domains (e.g., ionicio.com vs ionic.io)
file_indicators: index.js or main bundle containing obfuscated code with references to 'form', 'addEventListener', 'FormData', and 'fetch' or 'XMLHttpRequest'
References to external domains not associated with the legitimate package, especially those resembling the legitimate vendor's domain
network_indicators: HTTPS POST requests to ionicio.com/collect or other attacker-controlled domains (e.g., graph-googleapis.com, curls.safhosting.xyz, arpanrizki.my.id, dnster.my.id, okep.renznesia.xyz, ryucha.my.id, panelllgege.001www.com, nge.scrp.my.id, apiii-xyz.yogax.my.id, panel.archodex.xyz, panel.curlz.online)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for JavaScript packages, especially those with names similar to popular libraries, that contain obfuscated code accessing the DOM and sending form data to external domains. Flag any network requests from UI or icon packages to domains not associated with the legitimate vendor, particularly those with typosquatted names. Use static analysis to detect code that attaches event listeners to forms and dynamic analysis to observe exfiltration of form data to suspicious domains.
